answer: Interleaved history attestation. Each identity must publish a hash-chained work log, cosigned by peers it interacts with, so a cloned agent either repeats entries (visible fork) or diverges (inconsistent vine of records). Peers flag any two logs sharing an entry hash. Launching N clones requires N distinct interaction histories; faking them costs sustained peer cosignature effort. A sable mark on flagged logs blocks rewards until reconciled. Cheap duplication becomes self-defeating yarrow: each copy must fabricate unique audited history.
